prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a provider is reloaded from persistent storage (process restart), `OAuthContext.token_expiry_time` is never recomputed from the stored token's `expires_in`, so `is_token_valid()` treats a stale/expired stored token as still valid. This causes the proactive refresh branch in `async_auth_flow` to be skipped, and every access-token expiry after a restart forces a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a provider is reloaded from persistent storage (process restart), `OAuthContext.token_expiry_time` is never recomputed from the stored token's `expires_in`, so `is_token_valid()` treats a stale/expired stored token as still valid. This causes the proactive refresh branch in `async_auth_flow` to be skipped, and every access-token expiry after a restart forces a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1784 fixes the actual root cause with a 4-line change in `_initialize()` that recomputes `token_expiry_time` from the stored token's `expires_in`, restoring the invariant that `is_token_valid()` and the existing proactive-refresh branch already rely on elsewhere in the file; it also adds a dedicated `expired_tokens` fixture/test and removes the `# pragma: no cover` on `_initialize`, showing the fixed path is now exercised. #2875's own inline comment names this exact same root cause ('provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time') but only works around it reactively inside the 401 branch of `async_auth_flow`, leaving `token_expiry_time` itself still wrong for any other caller of `is_token_valid()`/`current_tokens`. Once #1784 lands, the proactive-refresh branch #2875's comment refers to already fires correctly, making #2875's added 401 fallback redundant for this bug.

prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both modify the write_stream memory-object-stream buffer size in stdio_server(), targeting the same underlying issue: with an unbuffered (rendezvous) write stream, a handler's send() blocks until the stdout_writer task both receives AND finishes flushing the prior message, so a handler can't queue its final response while an earlier notification (e.g. progress) is still being written to stdout. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both modify the write_stream memory-object-stream buffer size in stdio_server(), targeting the same underlying issue: with an unbuffered (rendezvous) write stream, a handler's send() blocks until the stdout_writer task both receives AND finishes flushing the prior message, so a handler can't queue its final response while an earlier notification (e.g. progress) is still being written to stdout. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 2654 fixes the bug by default by hardcoding the write-stream buffer to 1, so every caller benefits immediately without extra configuration, and it ships a targeted regression test (a BlockingStdout fixture that simulates a slow flush while a second message is queued) that directly exercises the notification-interleaving failure. 2215 only adds optional read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size parameters defaulting to 0 (i.e., unchanged behavior), so the reported blocking bug remains present for any caller who doesn't explicitly opt in, and its test diff shows no equivalent scenario reproducing the interleaving bug.

prs.title: fix(client/auth): discover AS metadata before cold-start token refresh, with issuer-binding check
prs.author: app/claude
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: A reloaded/cold-started `OAuthClientProvider` has `context.oauth_metadata` as `None` in memory (it was only ever discovered, never persisted), so `_refresh_token()` can't resolve the authorization server's token endpoint without rediscovering it, breaking or slowing down token refresh right after a restart. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: A reloaded/cold-started `OAuthClientProvider` has `context.oauth_metadata` as `None` in memory (it was only ever discovered, never persisted), so `_refresh_token()` can't resolve the authorization server's token endpoint without rediscovering it, breaking or slowing down token refresh right after a restart. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3263 solves this without touching the public `TokenStorage` Protocol: it performs discovery before the cold-start refresh and guards repeated rediscovery with a new `eager_discovery_attempted` flag on `OAuthContext`, and additionally adds an issuer-binding validation on the discovered metadata used for refresh, a security check not present in the other diff. #2492 instead adds two new optional methods (`get_oauth_metadata`/`set_oauth_metadata`) to the `TokenStorage` Protocol; because the defaults are no-ops, the fix only takes effect for storage backends that are updated to implement persistence, and the shown diff doesn't include such an implementation, whereas #3263's in-memory rediscovery-with-guard works transparently for every existing storage backend.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395's fix is fully contained in _handle_reconnection: it builds a properly-typed JSONRPCError (INTERNAL_ERROR) tied to the specific request id and sends it via ctx.read_stream_writer, so only the affected request resolves with an error while the rest of the session keeps running. #3098 only adds a standalone _unwrap_exception helper with no visible call site wiring it into the reconnection path in the diff, and its approach of raising a bare StreamableHTTPError out of a task group risks tearing down the whole task group (collateral impact on unrelated in-flight requests) rather than failing just the one pending request. #3098 also bundles an unrelated stylistic change (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` → `from __future__ import annotations`) that has nothing to do with the reconnection bug, making it a less focused change.

clusters.pick_reason: 2962 guards the comparison with has_tool_results so this case no longer raises at all, and its regression test docstring cites SEP-1577 directly ('tool_result blocks MUST be preceded by a tool_use block, but there is NO requirement that a tool_use MUST be followed by a tool_result') as the spec basis for treating this as valid, not an error. 3053 touches the identical condition but keeps the raise, only swapping in a clearer message ('tool_use blocks must be followed by matching tool_result blocks') and its test asserts a ValueError IS raised for the same input 2962's test asserts should pass silently - the two test suites are mutually exclusive and can't both pass against one implementation. 3053's diff doesn't reference SEP-1577 or otherwise argue the raise is spec-mandated, whereas 2962's change is the smaller, single-condition fix and comes with the spec citation backing the behavioral change.

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a provider is reloaded from persistent storage (process restart), `OAuthContext.token_expiry_time` is never recomputed from the stored token's `expires_in`, so `is_token_valid()` treats a stale/expired stored token as still valid. This causes the proactive refresh branch in `async_auth_flow` to be skipped, and every access-token expiry after a restart forces a full interactive re-authorization instead of a silent refresh. (2 PRs)

members.cluster_pick_reason: #1784 fixes the actual root cause with a 4-line change in `_initialize()` that recomputes `token_expiry_time` from the stored token's `expires_in`, restoring the invariant that `is_token_valid()` and the existing proactive-refresh branch already rely on elsewhere in the file; it also adds a dedicated `expired_tokens` fixture/test and removes the `# pragma: no cover` on `_initialize`, showing the fixed path is now exercised. #2875's own inline comment names this exact same root cause ('provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time') but only works around it reactively inside the 401 branch of `async_auth_flow`, leaving `token_expiry_time` itself still wrong for any other caller of `is_token_valid()`/`current_tokens`. Once #1784 lands, the proactive-refresh branch #2875's comment refers to already fires correctly, making #2875's added 401 fallback redundant for this bug.

clusters.pick_reason: #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() generalizes the skip condition to any union whose members are all in a simple-type set (str, int, float, bool, NoneType) — this covers str|None as well as str|int, str|bool, etc. #3056's _is_optional_str() only special-cases the str|None union specifically, so it doesn't cover the broader union cases #2032 handles. #3056's one edge case not covered by #2032 is a union member wrapped in Annotated (e.g. Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None), which #2032's frozenset membership check misses since an Annotated type object won't match the literal `str` entry in _SIMPLE_TYPES — that gap could be folded into #2032 via a follow-up unwrap step if needed.

clusters.pick_reason: 2654 fixes the bug by default by hardcoding the write-stream buffer to 1, so every caller benefits immediately without extra configuration, and it ships a targeted regression test (a BlockingStdout fixture that simulates a slow flush while a second message is queued) that directly exercises the notification-interleaving failure. 2215 only adds optional read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size parameters defaulting to 0 (i.e., unchanged behavior), so the reported blocking bug remains present for any caller who doesn't explicitly opt in, and its test diff shows no equivalent scenario reproducing the interleaving bug.

members.author: yaowubarbara

clusters.pick_reason: #2395's fix is fully contained in _handle_reconnection: it builds a properly-typed JSONRPCError (INTERNAL_ERROR) tied to the specific request id and sends it via ctx.read_stream_writer, so only the affected request resolves with an error while the rest of the session keeps running. #3098 only adds a standalone _unwrap_exception helper with no visible call site wiring it into the reconnection path in the diff, and its approach of raising a bare StreamableHTTPError out of a task group risks tearing down the whole task group (collateral impact on unrelated in-flight requests) rather than failing just the one pending request. #3098 also bundles an unrelated stylistic change (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` → `from __future__ import annotations`) that has nothing to do with the reconnection bug, making it a less focused change.

clusters.pick_reason: #3263 solves this without touching the public `TokenStorage` Protocol: it performs discovery before the cold-start refresh and guards repeated rediscovery with a new `eager_discovery_attempted` flag on `OAuthContext`, and additionally adds an issuer-binding validation on the discovered metadata used for refresh, a security check not present in the other diff. #2492 instead adds two new optional methods (`get_oauth_metadata`/`set_oauth_metadata`) to the `TokenStorage` Protocol; because the defaults are no-ops, the fix only takes effect for storage backends that are updated to implement persistence, and the shown diff doesn't include such an implementation, whereas #3263's in-memory rediscovery-with-guard works transparently for every existing storage backend.

clusters.pick_reason: 2962 guards the comparison with has_tool_results so this case no longer raises at all, and its regression test docstring cites SEP-1577 directly ('tool_result blocks MUST be preceded by a tool_use block, but there is NO requirement that a tool_use MUST be followed by a tool_result') as the spec basis for treating this as valid, not an error. 3053 touches the identical condition but keeps the raise, only swapping in a clearer message ('tool_use blocks must be followed by matching tool_result blocks') and its test asserts a ValueError IS raised for the same input 2962's test asserts should pass silently - the two test suites are mutually exclusive and can't both pass against one implementation. 3053's diff doesn't reference SEP-1577 or otherwise argue the raise is spec-mandated, whereas 2962's change is the smaller, single-condition fix and comes with the spec citation backing the behavioral change.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a quote-aware comma-splitting tokenizer, but #3041 splits the *entire* header value into top-level segments first and then isolates the Bearer challenge's auth-params via scheme-prefix matching (_extract_bearer_auth_params), so it correctly handles headers with multiple challenges (e.g. 'Digest ..., Bearer ...'). #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead finds the first space in the header and tokenizes everything after it as params, with no visible scheme-boundary check in the shown diff, so it risks lumping params from a second challenge into the Bearer param list on multi-challenge headers.
